stories.headline: 'Failed socialist state': Deep blue state’s lone GOP congressman reveals secret to winning as Democrats sweep
stories.note: A Republican who keeps winning in deep-blue territory offers the GOP a playbook for clawing back ground.
body: Rep. Cliff Bentz, Oregon's only Republican in Congress, held his eastern Oregon seat for a fourth term with about 61% of the vote, winning by more than 70,000 votes even as a Democratic wave swept the country.

In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, Bentz said his voters wanted someone dependable on protecting business and pushing back against what he calls Oregon's slide toward becoming a failed state. He blamed "crazy, crazy Democrat policies emanating out of Salem" for the damage.

Bentz pointed to Oregon's 9.9% top income tax rate, a 7.6% top corporate rate and a corporate activity tax, plus newer rules like mandatory advance work schedules for big retail, hospitality and food-service employers, as burdens that critics say are choking the state's economy.

With Democrats set to hold large majorities in both chambers, Bentz argued Republicans in the minority should spend the next two years spotlighting the economic fallout of Democratic policy and presenting a clear alternative, essentially telling voters that if they want more of the same, they can keep voting for it.

Why it matters: After a bruising midterm, Bentz's district is proof that a message built on taxes, regulation and cost of living can still win big, and he's offering it as a roadmap for the GOP's comeback.

stories.headline: Trump to confront Newsom over plan to spare 548 death row inmates, including notorious child killers
stories.note: Trump stands with victims' families against Newsom's plan to spare 548 condemned killers, a fight voters have sided with twice.
body: President Trump is set to appear Monday afternoon at the Justice Department with Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel to condemn Gov. Gavin Newsom's plan to commute all 548 death sentences in California to life without parole, the White House told Fox News Digital.

Families of murder victims are expected to attend. The White House circulated a list of 20 notorious killers who would benefit, including Marcus Wesson, who murdered nine relatives in Fresno; Richard Allen Davis, the killer of 12-year-old Polly Klaas; and Isauro Aguirre, convicted of torturing 8-year-old Gabriel Fernandez to death.

White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said Newsom is "failing the victims and their families" and told him to stop playing politics with public safety. Newsom's office pointed to his earlier letter, in which he said he respects voters keeping the death penalty but believes clemency power exists for moments like this.

The commutations aren't in effect yet. For 382 of the inmates, California law requires a state Supreme Court recommendation, and prosecutors and victims' advocates have asked the court to block the plan. The court is taking additional briefs through Tuesday, and Newsom wants a decision before he leaves office in January.

Why it matters: California voters rejected repealing the death penalty in 2012 and 2016. By siding with victims' families against Newsom's lame-duck clemency push, Trump puts a likely 2028 Democratic contender on the wrong side of voters on crime.

stories.headline: New York Dem addresses bizarre 'lizard people' claims after viral clip behind Mamdani
stories.note: A viral 'lizard people' moment at Mamdani's Rikers closure presser turns his plan to shrink NYC's jail population into a punchline.
body: Democratic Assemblyman Jordan J.G. Wright of Harlem found himself at the center of an internet frenzy after a clip from Mayor Zohran Mamdani's Friday press conference appeared to show his eyes rolling back in an odd circular motion as he stood behind the mayor.
The video revived the old 'reptilian' conspiracy theory online, with users on X and Reddit joking, or insisting, that Wright wasn't human.

Wright told the New York Post he had no idea what was going on in the video, insisted he is human, and pointed to his legislative work, including $4 million for a Harlem environmental justice center. "I can't speak to any reptiles or aliens," he said.

The press conference itself was about Mamdani's plan to cut the city's jail population by 2,500 inmates over five years and close Rikers Island by 2032, moving roughly 4,100 remaining detainees to four smaller borough-based jails.
Why it matters: The viral sideshow is embarrassing, but the bigger story underneath is Mamdani's push to shrink the jail population, a soft-on-crime move that Republicans can keep in the spotlight.

stories.headline: Trump says it would be 'hard' to work with Chuck Schumer: 'He will fail again'
stories.note: Trump piles on a Senate Democratic leader already fending off a challenge from his own left flank.
body: President Trump said on Truth Social Sunday that it would be "very hard" to work with Sen. Chuck Schumer if Democrats make him Senate majority leader again next year, predicting he "will fail again."
Trump called Schumer one of the worst leaders in history and said his push of the Russia hoax and other "scams" helped make Trump's 2024 win easy.

Schumer faces a challenge from Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, who represents the party's more radical wing and has support from Sen. Bernie Sanders, Sen. Jeff Merkley, Sens.-elect Abdul El-Sayed and Peggy Flanagan, and, as of last week, Sen. Elissa Slotkin.
Fox News Digital has reported Schumer has 15 senators in his corner so far. He has stayed quiet but confident, saying he welcomes the discussion and has the votes to keep the job.

Why it matters: Senate Democrats are heading into their new majority with a leadership fight between an old-guard leader and the progressive wing, and Trump is making clear Schumer won't get an easy partner.

stories.headline: Progressives unveil $25 minimum wage push to solve affordability crisis despite economist inflation warning
stories.note: Progressives' $25 wage plan hands Republicans an easy inflation and small-business argument.
body: The Congressional Progressive Caucus is pushing to raise the federal minimum wage from $7.25 to $25 an hour, more than tripling it, with backers calling the current wage a "remnant of slavery."

Rep. Everton Blair Jr., D-Ga., told Fox News Digital $25 should be the floor, indexed to inflation and higher in expensive areas. He acknowledged inflation concerns but said workers' earnings have to rise. Rep. Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., said corporations simply don't want to pay livable wages.

Heritage Foundation chief economist E.J. Antoni warned that setting a wage floor above the market creates a surplus of labor, which he said shows up as unemployment, with effects reaching well beyond big cities.

Progressives say they expect support from Democratic leadership as the party builds its affordability agenda for the next Congress. The Living Wage for All coalition cited its own polling claiming most Republicans back the idea. Jeffries and the White House didn't respond to requests for comment.

Why it matters: A $25 national wage would hit small businesses and lower-cost states hardest, and it gives Republicans a clear argument that the new Democratic majority's 'affordability' plan would actually raise prices and kill jobs.

stories.headline: DHS, Dem officials clash after ICE arrest at Seattle airport
stories.note: DHS pushes back hard on Democrats trying to obstruct immigration enforcement in Seattle.
body: ICE officers arrested two people on a Seattle-Tacoma airport jetway Saturday morning as passengers boarded an Alaska Airlines flight. DHS said the target, Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, is a Mexican national who overstayed his visa, and that other travelers got in the way.

DHS said a second woman, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, threw hot coffee at the agents and will be charged with assaulting a federal officer. Her attorney disputed DHS's description, saying she entered legally and was in the process of adjusting her status after marrying a U.S. citizen.

Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson declared ICE "completely and totally out of control" and said he'd urge every airline at the airport to tell ICE to leave, without mentioning the alleged assault. Reps. Pramila Jayapal and Adam Smith and Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson also blasted the agents.

DHS answered that assaulting and obstructing officers is a felony and will be prosecuted, citing large increases in assaults, vehicle attacks and death threats against its officers. "This violence must end," the department posted.

Why it matters: Democrats ran on affordability, but Jayapal is already vowing to use the new majority to rein in ICE, setting up a fight over immigration enforcement that Republicans see as favorable ground.

stories.headline: 'Crazy': Moderates fear Dem leadership promised far-left reparations and ICE demands in turn of votes
stories.note: Moderate Democrats worry their leaders cut deals with the far left on reparations and ICE, a split the GOP can exploit.
body: Progressive House Democrats say they expect party leaders to give their far-left agenda, including reparations and abolishing ICE, a hearing under the new majority, alarming moderates who want the focus on costs.

Newly elected Caucus Chairman Ted Lieu told Fox News Digital he's open to "discussions on everything," including reparations, abolishing ICE, Medicare for All and expanded Temporary Protected Status. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez said she and Speaker-nominee Hakeem Jeffries share ground on Medicaid and public housing.
Moderates pushed back. Rep. Josh Gottheimer said the agenda is about costs and rejected defunding police, open borders or abolishing the Senate, saying the DSA "have their own agenda."

One Democratic lawmaker, speaking anonymously, called the idea of leadership adopting the progressive wish list "crazy" and suggested Lieu and Jeffries were signaling openness only to avoid opposition in leadership elections. Jeffries and Rep. Ayanna Pressley didn't respond to requests for comment.

Why it matters: Before the new majority even takes over, Democrats are split between moderates and a left wing pushing reparations and ending ICE, which gives Republicans a ready-made message for 2028.
